description:
Records money received against threads and produces billed-versus-received statements.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD AMOUNT [-c CUR] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE ...] — record a receipt
  list [THREAD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — list payments
  statement [--thread T] [--since D] [--until D] [--as-of D] [--pdf PATH] [--json] — billed vs received, by thread and currency
  show ID [--json] — show one payment
  edit ID [--amount N] [-c CUR] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE ...] — change fields of a payment
  rm ID -y — delete a payment

Flags:
  log:
    -c, --currency CUR  ISO code. Defaults to the thread's currency.
    -d, --date D        date received, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.
    -t, --time HH:MM    time received. Default now.
    -a, --account A     account the money landed in
    -n, --note TEXT     free-text note; may be several words
  list:
    --since D / --until D  inclusive date bounds
    --json                 JSON output
  statement:
    --thread T             one thread only
    --since D / --until D  inclusive date bounds
    --as-of D              statement date; drives aging. Default today.
    --pdf PATH             render a PDF to PATH. Requires --thread.
    --json                 JSON output
  edit:
    --amount N  new amount
    -c, -d, -t, -a, -n  new currency, date, time, account, note
  rm:
    -y, --yes  required to confirm the delete

Args:
  THREAD  thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink
  AMOUNT  required in practice; a positive decimal
  ID      8-char payment id from `payments list`

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "15000.00", "-d", "2026-09-25", "-a", "Business cheque"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/SGB"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--pdf", "statement.pdf"]
  ["rm", "1a2b3c4d", "-y"]

Notes:
  Put the positionals first. -n takes several words, so pass it last.
  log queues a REF in the buffer, filed under the day the money was received. It reaches the thread's log on the next `buffer flush`.
  rm is permanent and needs -y.
  Exit code 1 means: a missing, invalid or non-positive amount; --pdf without --thread; or nothing to state for that thread.
